lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Scale 1 cm : 50 m. Map length 6 cm. What real distance?

FEEDBACK
300 m.

WATCH FOR
Forgetting to multiply by the scale leaves the map centimetres as if they were real metres.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Solve ten scale/map distance problems. Show map measure → × scale for each. Draw two simple grid routes.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Simple map scales convert measured map lengths to real distances; grid steps can also estimate paths.
materials: Optional: place-value chart or number line
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Solve ten scale/map distance problems. Show map measure → × scale for each. Draw two simple grid routes. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: new numbers solved with visible working for scale; key places/values named. Do not award marks for retyping the model.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample misconception: Forgetting to multiply by the scale leaves the map centimetres as if they were real metres.. Correction uses 300 m.. Why: restores accurate scale.

Parent: Likely misconception: Forgetting to multiply by the scale leaves the map centimetres as if they were real metres. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Solve one fresh problem that uses scale with different numbers from the worked model. Show working and name the places or values that matter.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Describe one likely mistake with scale, show corrected working, and say why the correction works.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept any mathematically valid solution that uses new numbers, shows working for scale, and names places/values. Reject copied model numbers. / Accept a named misconception about scale, corrected working, and a method reason. Reject vague “I was wrong” with no repair..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Scale 1 cm : 100 m. A path 4 cm on the map → 400 m real. Count grid units along a route then multiply by the scale.

TRY FIRST
Scale 1 cm : 50 m. Map length 6 cm. What real distance?

FEEDBACK
300 m.
teach_steps.explain:
Simple map scales convert measured map lengths to real distances; grid steps can also estimate paths.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Forgetting to multiply by the scale leaves the map centimetres as if they were real metres. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
